display.purpose: Page-level titles. One per view, set tight at -0.035em.

title.purpose: Section heads inside panels and on the floor.

body.purpose: Message text, field values, button labels.

label.purpose: Chips, keys, dense rail labels. Sentence case.

numeric.purpose: Counts, times and durations. Always tabular.

shadows.name: raise
shadows.purpose: Lightest lift. Secondary buttons and panels at rest.

shadows.name: panel
shadows.purpose: Raised interface surfaces that own their content.

shadows.name: room
shadows.purpose: A room platform sitting on the floor.

shadows.name: float
shadows.purpose: Popovers, dialogs, your own room, a hovered room.

shadows.name: lit
shadows.purpose: The 1px top-edge light. Never used alone; always with one of the four above.

shadows.name: contact
shadows.purpose: Tight anchor under a small object that must read as resting on a surface.

motion.name: ease-out-soft
motion.purpose: Default easing for every state and movement transition.

motion.name: ease-spring
motion.purpose: Reserved for things that should feel physical: a tile arriving, a popover opening.

motion.name: duration-state
motion.purpose: Hover, active, selection and other state changes.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single accented action on a surface. A lit gradient face, not a flat fill.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: linear-gradient(180deg, var(--color-brand-500, #c04170) 0%, var(--color-accent, #a62e5c) 100%); color: #fff; border: 1px solid var(--color-brand-700, #8e2450); border-radius: var(--radius-control, 10px); padding: 8px 14px; min-height: 36px; font-family: Geist, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 13.5px; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1.2; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgb(255 255 255 / 0.22), 0 1px 2px rgb(43 38 32 / 0.16); cursor: pointer; transition: background 140ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), box-shadow 140ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), transform 140ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { filter: brightness(0.975); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: translateY(1px) scale(0.985); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-focus-ring, #a62e5c); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: The default control. White surface, strong hairline, raise plus the 1px top light.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { background: var(--color-surface, #ffffff); color: var(--color-ink, #1a1713); border: 1px solid var(--color-hairline-strong, #d9d3c6); border-radius: var(--radius-control, 10px); padding: 8px 14px; min-height: 36px; font-family: Geist, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 13.5px; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1.2; box-shadow: 0 1px 1px rgb(43 38 32 / 0.04), 0 1px 3px rgb(43 38 32 / 0.05), inset 0 1px 0 rgb(255 255 255 / 0.75); cursor: pointer; transition: background 140ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), box-shadow 140ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), transform 140ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1); } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { filter: brightness(0.975); } .ds-btn-secondary:active { transform: translateY(1px) scale(0.985); } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-focus-ring, #a62e5c); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Panel
components.description: A raised interface surface: tonal step, layered shadow and the 1px top light, applied as a set.
components.html:
Today

Four meetings, two of them back to back.
components.css: .ds-panel { background: var(--color-surface, #ffffff); border: 1px solid var(--color-hairline, #e7e2d8); border-radius: var(--radius-panel, 16px); padding: 18px; box-shadow: 0 1px 1px rgb(43 38 32 / 0.04), 0 1px 3px rgb(43 38 32 / 0.05), inset 0 1px 0 rgb(255 255 255 / 0.75); font-family: Geist, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-panel-title { margin: 0 0 6px; font-size: 19px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: -0.025em; line-height: 1.2; color: var(--color-ink, #1a1713); } .ds-panel-body { margin: 0; font-size: 13.5px; line-height: 1.55; color: var(--color-ink-muted, #6e6659); }

components.name: Text Field
components.description: Label above, hint between, error below. A placeholder never stands in for a label.
components.html: Everyone in the workspace can see this.
components.css: .ds-field { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 6px; font-family: Geist, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-field-label { font-size: 12.5px; font-weight: 500; color: var(--color-ink, #1a1713); } .ds-field-hint { font-size: 12px; color: var(--color-ink-muted, #6e6659); } .ds-field-input { background: var(--color-surface, #ffffff); border: 1px solid var(--color-hairline-strong, #d9d3c6); border-radius: var(--radius-control, 10px); padding: 8px 11px; min-height: 36px; font-size: 13.5px; color: var(--color-ink, #1a1713); } .ds-field-input:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-focus-ring, #a62e5c); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Row Navigation Item
components.description: The shared row control: channels, presence rows, meeting rows, search results. Active is background plus colour, never colour alone.
components.html: generaldesignclients
components.css: .ds-nav { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 2px; font-family: Geist, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-nav-row { display: flex; align-items: center; padding: 6px 10px; min-height: 28px; border-radius: var(--radius-control, 10px); font-size: 13.5px; color: var(--color-ink-muted, #6e6659); text-decoration: none; transition: background 140ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), color 140ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1); } .ds-nav-row:hover { background: var(--color-surface-sunken, #f7f5f1); } .ds-nav-row[aria-current="true"] { background: var(--color-accent-soft, #fdf3f7); color: var(--color-ink-brand, #a62e5c); font-weight: 500; } .ds-nav-row:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-focus-ring, #a62e5c); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Chip
components.description: Fully rounded soft-tinted label. Never the only carrier of a status.
components.css: .ds-chip { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 4px; padding: 2px 8px; border-radius: 999px; font-family: Geist, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 11.5px; font-weight: 500; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-chip-neutral { background: var(--color-surface-sunken, #f7f5f1); color: var(--color-ink-muted, #6e6659); } .ds-chip-accent { background: var(--color-accent-soft, #fdf3f7); color: var(--color-ink-brand, #a62e5c); }

components.name: Avatar with Presence Mark
components.description: The atomic unit of presence. A tint lit from the upper left, with a mark whose SHAPE carries the state.
components.html: RM TK
components.css: .ds-avatar { position: relative; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 40px; height: 40px; border-radius: 999px; background: radial-gradient(circle at 32% 26%, #f4ece4, #eadfd3 78%); color: #5c4a38; font-family: Geist, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.01em; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgb(255 255 255 / 0.55), 0 1px 2px rgb(43 38 32 / 0.12); } .ds-avatar-offline { opacity: 0.55; box-shadow: none; } .ds-avatar-mark { position: absolute; right: -1px; bottom: -1px; line-height: 0; }

components.name: Room Platform
components.description: A room on the floor: a raised platform with the layered room shadow and the 1px top light, lifting 1px on hover.
components.css: .ds-floor { background: var(--color-floor, #efebe3); background-image: radial-gradient(120% 90% at 12% 0%, rgb(255 255 255 / 0.85) 0%, rgb(255 255 255 / 0) 62%), radial-gradient(circle at 1px 1px, rgb(154 146 132 / 0.22) 1px, transparent 0); background-size: auto, 24px 24px; padding: 28px; border-radius: 16px; } .ds-room { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 2px; width: 190px; padding: 10px; text-align: start; background: var(--color-floor-room, #ffffff); border: 1px solid var(--color-floor-room-stroke, #e7e2d8); border-radius: var(--radius-room, 22px); box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgb(43 38 32 / 0.04), 0 6px 14px -4px rgb(43 38 32 / 0.07), 0 18px 36px -14px rgb(43 38 32 / 0.09), inset 0 1px 0 rgb(255 255 255 / 0.75); cursor: pointer; font-family: Geist, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; transition: box-shadow 140ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), border-color 140ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), transform 140ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1); } .ds-room:hover { border-color: var(--color-paper-400, #d9d3c6); box-shadow: 0 2px 4px rgb(43 38 32 / 0.05), 0 12px 22px -6px rgb(43 38 32 / 0.11), 0 28px 56px -18px rgb(43 38 32 / 0.16), inset 0 1px 0 rgb(255 255 255 / 0.75); transform: translateY(-1px); } .ds-room:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-focus-ring, #a62e5c); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-room-name { font-size: 13.5px; font-weight: 600; color: var(--color-ink, #1a1713); } .ds-room-meta { font-size: 11.5px; color: var(--color-ink-muted, #6e6659); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }

components.name: Dimensional Floor Object
components.description: The Solid extrusion primitive every piece of furniture is built from: contact shadow, side face, lit top face, 1px leading highlight.
components.css: .ds-solid { position: relative; display: block; width: 74px; height: 39px; } .ds-solid-contact { position: absolute; left: 2px; right: 2px; top: 34px; height: 8px; border-radius: 50%; background: rgb(43 38 32 / 0.13); filter: blur(4px); } .ds-solid-side { position: absolute; inset-inline: 0; top: 7px; height: 32px; background: var(--mat-oak-side, #c9b896); border-radius: var(--radius-object, 5px); } .ds-solid-top { position: absolute; inset-inline: 0; top: 0; height: 32px; background: linear-gradient(150deg, var(--mat-oak-top, #efe4d2) 0%, var(--mat-oak, #e2d3bb) 78%); border-radius: var(--radius-object, 5px); box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgb(255 255 255 / 0.6); }

components.name: Count Badge
components.description: Unread and mention counts. Tabular so a sidebar never jitters.
components.css: .ds-count { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; min-width: 18px; height: 18px; padding: 0 6px; border-radius: 999px; background: var(--color-paper-400, #d9d3c6); color: var(--color-paper-900, #2b2620); font-family: Geist, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 600; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-count-mention { background: var(--color-accent, #a62e5c); color: #ffffff; }

narrative.overview:
Somion HQ is a warm daylight office rendered as software. The world is light, friendly and unhurried, because people sit inside it for eight hours; nothing here is a conceptual statement. What separates it from a plain beige admin panel is not more colour, it is craft: crisp value steps between surfaces, an elevation scale that is genuinely used, a type ramp with a real top end, and a single direction of light obeyed by every raised object in the product, interface chrome and drawn furniture alike.

The floor is the signature. Rooms are raised platforms on a warm ground with ambient daylight falling from the upper left, and the furniture inside them is built rather than drawn: each piece is an extrusion with a contact shadow, a darker side face, a lit top face and a 1px leading highlight. Because those four moves are identical on all fifteen piece kinds, a floor of them reads as designed instead of assembled. Every object is token-coloured CSS, so it restyles with the brand and there is no asset to redraw.

Saturation is a scarce, governed resource. Six presence hues are the only saturated colour in the product; the rose brand sits far enough from all of them that it can never be mistaken for a status; furniture materials, avatar tints and room zones are all desaturated warm neutrals that stay above muted ink in value, so a person always outranks the room they are standing in. Density is high but not airless: 14px base body on a 4px rhythm, tabular numerals wherever counts change.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper neutrals with deliberately separable value steps, so surfaces stack without a border on every edge.
Presence is the only saturated material; six states, six hues, six distinct mark shapes.
One light direction for the whole product, from the upper left.
Elevation always travels as a set: tonal step, layered shadow, 1px top light.
Dimensional floor furniture built from one extrusion primitive and six material triplets.
Light theme only, as an explicit decision.

rules.name: The Presence Owns Saturation Rule
rules.body: The six presence hues are the only saturated colour in the product. Nothing decorative, illustrative, or furniture-related may reuse them, and nothing else may reach their chroma.

rules.name: The Brand Is Not A Status Rule
rules.body: The rose sits at hue 337, at least 58 degrees from every presence hue. Never place the accent where a status mark could be expected, and never introduce an accent variant that closes that gap.

rules.name: The Never Colour Alone Rule
rules.body: Every one of the six states carries a distinct mark shape and a text label alongside its hue. Offline is a hollow ring, not a pale fill. A state that only differs by colour is not shipped.

rules.name: The Three-Background Rule
rules.body: A presence mark must clear 3:1 as a UI component against all three surfaces it can land on - ground, floor and white room surface - not only the one in the current mock. Any new presence value is tested against all three before it exists.

rules.name: The Value-Not-Hue Zoning Rule
rules.body: Room zones separate from the floor by value on the warm ramp, never by hue. A cool tint on this world reads as a mistake, and a desaturated presence hue reads as a status.

rules.name: The Sequential Delivery Rule
rules.body: The magnitude ramp's two lightest steps fall below 3:1 by nature. It therefore never ships alone: always with a table view, per-cell values on hover and focus, and a separating gap between cells. The ramp is not darkened to hide the finding.

rules.name: The Real Top End Rule
rules.body: Display and title are set tight (-0.035em, -0.025em) and are the only steps allowed to break 15px. A screen where everything sits between 11px and 13.5px reads as flat regardless of its colour.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Any number that changes in place - counts, times, durations - carries tabular numerals, so a sidebar never jitters.

rules.name: The Self-Carrying Heading Rule
rules.body: Section headings carry their own weight. No eyebrow, no kicker, no section number, no floating explainer beside the title.

rules.name: The Designed Floor Plan Rule
rules.body: Room layouts are hand-composed per room - desks in rows with circulation between them, a table centred under a wall screen - never generated. A randomised floor plan looks randomised.

rules.name: The One Light Direction Rule
rules.body: The whole product is lit from the upper left, once. Raised interface surfaces take the 1px top light; drawn floor objects take a lit top face over a darker extruded side. There is no second light source, and no object may cast a shadow that contradicts the first.

rules.name: The Elevation Travels As A Set Rule
rules.body: Tonal step + layered shadow + 1px top light are one decision, applied together. Applying one without the others is exactly what makes depth read as inconsistent.

rules.name: The Person Outranks The Furniture Rule
rules.body: Materials stay above muted ink in value and add no saturation, so a person - white ring, dark initial, saturated presence lamp, name plate - always wins the depth contest against the room. On hover, rooms lift by 1px; people scale by 7%. Furniture that competes with people defeats the product.

rules.name: The Decorative Layer Is Silent Rule
rules.body: The whole furniture layer is aria-hidden and non-interactive. It never enters the accessibility tree, never intercepts a click meant for the room, and never adds a tab stop.

rules.name: The Two Radius Scales Rule
rules.body: Interface radius (10 / 16 / 22 / full) and object radius (2 / 3 / 5 / 7) never cross. Picking from the wrong scale is the fastest way to make a drawn object look like a button, or a button look like a tile.

dos: Do apply elevation as a set - tonal step, layered shadow, and the 1px top light - or don't raise the surface at all.
Do light every new raised object from the upper left: a lit top face over a darker side for drawn objects, the 1px top light for interface surfaces.
Do give every new presence-bearing state a distinct mark shape and a text label, and test its colour against ground, floor and white surface.
Do separate floor zones by value on the warm ramp (#efebe3 / #f6f3ed / #f4eee2 / #faf8f4 / #ffffff).
Do pick radius from the correct scale: 10 / 16 / 22 / full for interface, 2 / 3 / 5 / 7 for drawn objects.
Do ship the sequential ramp with a table view, per-cell values on hover and focus, and a separating gap.
Do use tabular numerals for any number that updates in place.
Do keep furniture and avatar tints above muted ink in value, so the person outranks the room.
Do treat light-theme-only as an explicit decision for an eight-hour daylight operate surface, declared with color-scheme: light.
donts: Don't put a raw hex value in feature code. Every colour comes from a token; the single sanctioned exception is Excalidraw's initialData, whose API takes literals rather than CSS variables.
Don't reuse a presence hue for anything decorative, or introduce a new saturated colour anywhere outside the six states.
Don't place the rose accent where a status could be expected, or add an accent variant that narrows the 58-degree gap to the presence hues.
Don't convey status, activity or selection by colour alone.
Don't tint the floor or a room cool, or use a desaturated presence hue as a surface.
Don't darken the sequential ramp's light steps to make a contrast finding disappear; fix it in delivery, not in the ramp.
Don't give an interactive element a hover state without an active and a :focus-visible state, and never remove the focus ring.
Don't add an eyebrow, kicker or section number above a heading; headings carry their own weight.
Don't let furniture gain saturation, contrast or height that competes with a person standing next to it.
Don't generate floor layouts procedurally; a floor plan is designed.
